sections.category: OpenAI buys Ona, the rebranded Gitpod, to move Codex agents off the laptop and into persistent cloud sandboxes that keep multi-day coding runs alive after the developer's machine shuts down

bullets.body: OpenAI announced on June 11 that it is acquiring Ona, the German startup formerly known as Gitpod, for undisclosed terms (pending regulatory approval), folding the Ona team into the Codex group, per [SiliconANGLE - OpenAI acquires AI agent orchestration startup Ona](https://siliconangle.com/2026/06/11/openai-acquires-ai-agent-orchestration-startup-ona/). Ona's product runs coding agents inside persistent cloud-based sandboxes rather than on a developer's local machine, so an agent task that takes hours or days keeps executing even after the workstation is powered off - and the developer can review the run and give feedback when they come back to it; OpenAI frames the deal as letting Codex (now past 5 million weekly users, and already capable of extended sessions via GPT-5.1-Codex-Max) reliably carry long-running, multi-day software tasks to completion, per [The Tech Portal - OpenAI agrees to acquire AI cloud startup 'Ona', team will join Codex division](https://thetechportal.com/2026/06/11/openai-agrees-to-acquire-ai-cloud-startup-ona-team-will-join-codex-division/). The strategic read, surfaced more explicitly in European trade coverage, is that the durable cloud-sandbox layer is precisely the workflow Anthropic currently dominates inside enterprises, and OpenAI is buying the infrastructure and talent to contest it, per [Techzine - As Anthropic claims the enterprise, OpenAI fights back with Ona deal](https://www.techzine.eu/news/devops/142087/as-anthropic-claims-the-enterprise-openai-fights-back-with-ona-deal/). This pushes the coding-agent contest down a layer: the differentiator is shifting from raw model capability toward who owns the durable, restart-surviving execution substrate the agent runs in - the same problem space that suspended-conversation and cloud-sandbox primitives have been circling, now consolidated by acquisition rather than built in-house.

sections.category: Zyphra open-sources Zamba2-VL, a 1.2B/2.7B/7B family of Mamba2-Transformer hybrid vision-language models under Apache 2.0 that cut time-to-first-token by roughly an order of magnitude and punch far above their weight on visual counting

bullets.body: On June 12 Zyphra released Zamba2-VL, a family of open vision-language models at 1.2B, 2.7B, and 7B parameters under a permissive Apache 2.0 license, with checkpoints on Hugging Face and inference code in a custom transformers fork, per [MarkTechPost - Zyphra releases Zamba2-VL hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/06/12/zyphra-release-zamba2-vl-hybrid-mamba2-transformer-vision-language-models-that-cut-time-to-first-token-by-about-an-order-of-magnitude/). Architecturally it is a departure from the standard transformer VLM recipe: the language backbone pairs Mamba2 state-space layers with a small number of shared transformer blocks, and the vision side reuses the Vision Transformer from Qwen2.5-VL wired in through a two-layer MLP adapter; Zyphra measures roughly an order-of-magnitude lower time-to-first-token versus comparable transformer VLMs on 32K-token prefill, which is the latency regime that matters for local, on-device document and screen understanding. On accuracy the small models are not just competitive but strong on perception-heavy tasks - the 2.7B variant posts PixMoCount 82.5, CountBenchQA 87.5, and DocVQA 90.9, and at 1.2B it reaches PixMoCount 62.5, nearly double the transformer-based InternVL3.5-1B (32.8), per [Zyphra - Zamba2-VL](https://www.zyphra.com/our-work/zamba2-vl). The release matters as a concrete open-weight data point that the SSM-hybrid backbone, already pitched on cost and throughput, can carry multimodal perception at the 1-7B sizes that actually fit on local hardware - putting genuinely fast, fully-licensed VLMs in reach for edge and embedded inference rather than only API endpoints.

citations.label: MarkTechPost - Zyphra releases Zamba2-VL hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models

sections.category: Moonshot ships Kimi Work, a downloadable desktop agent that runs a 300-sub-agent swarm locally on the open-weight Kimi K2.6 - the same model Unsloth already serves on-device via 2-bit dynamic quantization, sharpening the local-vs-cloud line for autonomous agents

bullets.body: Moonshot AI launched Kimi Work on June 12, a downloadable desktop application (macOS on Apple silicon and Windows) rather than a web chat: the user states goals in plain language and the agent acts directly on the machine, coordinating an Agent Swarm that scales to about 300 sub-agents running in parallel, driving the user's logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension (reusing existing sessions and cookies), and firing scheduled jobs via a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle for overnight runs, per [MarkTechPost - Moonshot AI launches Kimi Work, a local desktop agent on Kimi K2.6 with a 300-sub-agent swarm](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/06/12/moonshot-ai-launches-kimi-work-a-local-desktop-agent-reportedly-running-on-kimi-k2-6-with-a-300-sub-agent-agent-swarm/). It reads mounted local folders, runs Python in the background, and leaves original files untouched unless changes are approved - a system-level, local-first take on the autonomous worker that contrasts with the cloud-sandbox direction OpenAI just bought into. The engine underneath is Kimi K2.6, Moonshot's open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model (about 32B active parameters per token, 256K context) released April 20, and the local-execution story is reinforced by the fact that the same weights are already runnable on-device through Unsloth, whose Dynamic 2.0 quantization ships a 2-bit (UD-Q2_K_XL) build of K2.6 alongside near-lossless variants for high-RAM workstations, per [Unsloth - Kimi K2.6: How to run locally](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/kimi-k2.6). Taken together the day's signal in the agent layer is a fork in deployment philosophy: persistent off-machine sandboxes (OpenAI/Ona) on one side, and an always-on local swarm operating on the user's own files and browser session (Kimi Work) on the other, both betting on long-horizon autonomy but disagreeing on where the agent should live.

Unsloth - Kimi K2.6: How to run locally

sections.category: The AI-lab IPO race goes concrete: Anthropic's confidential S-1 (June 1) and OpenAI's set the two largest labs on a collision course toward public markets, the same week SpaceX prices the largest IPO in history at $135 a share - and OpenAI opens a no-new-procurement path to its models through Oracle cloud credits

bullets.body: The frontier-lab path to public markets firmed up this week. Anthropic confidentially filed a draft Form S-1 with the SEC on June 1 - on the back of the $65B round that set its $965B post-money valuation and an annualized revenue run-rate that crossed $47B (more than tripling since February) - explicitly setting up an IPO season that pits it against OpenAI, which is targeting a raise of at least $60B at a valuation of up to $1 trillion and is expected to list by year's end, per [SiliconANGLE - Anthropic confidentially files for IPO amid rapid growth](https://siliconangle.com/2026/06/01/anthropic-confidentially-files-ipo-amid-rapid-growth/). The backdrop turned concrete on June 11 when SpaceX officially priced 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece to raise about $75B - the largest IPO in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut - with the stock set to trade on Nasdaq under SPCX, a print that resets the ceiling for how much capital the public markets will absorb for a single high-multiple technology name, per [ZeroHedge - SpaceX Prices Biggest Ever IPO At $135 Per Share](https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/spacex-prices-biggest-ever-ipo-135-share). On the commercial-distribution side the same stretch, OpenAI and Oracle moved to let Oracle Cloud Infrastructure customers apply eligible Oracle Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models and Codex - so enterprises with existing Oracle commitments can route AI workloads to OpenAI without opening a new procurement path or disrupting existing governance, with availability framed for the coming weeks, per [StartupHub.ai - OpenAI teams up with Oracle Cloud](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/openai-teams-up-with-oracle-cloud). The corporate-activity throughline is that the labs are simultaneously pursuing equity-market scale and frictionless enterprise distribution - testing both how much the public market will fund AI and how cleanly that compute can be sold through incumbent cloud channels.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: WWDC closes today, Databricks' 30,000-person Data + AI Summit opens Monday at Moscone, and the summer calendar spans security (Confidential Computing, Black Hat AI) and chip (AMD Advancing AI, Hot Chips) tracks

bullets.body: With Apple's WWDC26 reaching its final day today, the still-upcoming AI calendar worth planning attendance around continues across three tracks. On the mainstream developer/data side, the Databricks Data + AI Summit opens June 15-18 across Moscone North, West and South (30,000-plus in person from 150-plus countries, 800-plus sessions spanning AI agents, data engineering and governance; keynotes from Databricks' co-founders plus OpenAI's Greg Brockman and a recorded Satya Nadella fireside, with the Chainsmokers at Oracle Park on June 17), per [San Francisco Tribune - Databricks brings Data + AI Summit back to San Francisco](https://thesanfranciscotribune.com/databricks-brings-data-ai-summit-back-to-san-francisco-as-enterprise-ai-event-calendar-grows/); and the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 29-July 2 at Moscone West with 29 tracks across 6,000-plus attendees and 300 speakers, including dedicated Inference and Security tracks, per [AI Red Team - AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai-redteam.com/insights/worldsfair26/). On the AI-security track, the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, on confidential agents and secure AI workflows, with speakers from AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Samsung and UC Berkeley); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay; and in Las Vegas, Black Hat USA's single-day AI Summit (August 4, inside the August 1-6 conference) and DEF CON's AI Village anchor the agentic red-teaming calendar, with OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Francisco November 2-6; Zenity's practitioner-led AI Agent Security Summit - which the user tracks - has confirmed a 2026 global expansion to New York, London and APAC, with dates still worth monitoring. On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD has locked its Advancing AI 2026 event to July 22-23 at the San Francisco Moscone Center (Instinct MI400-series availability expected, with an MI450 unveil anticipated); Hot Chips 2026 takes Stanford's Memorial Auditorium August 23-25 with early registration open through July 31; and the AI Infra Summit runs September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center (8,000 attendees, 400-plus speakers across compute, AI data centers and physical AI). Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas.
